mainPoints.explanation: Cloud-native and microservices have increased the number of services to over 3,000 and monitoring items to tens of millions, making it difficult for traditional models to meet the "1, 5, 10" service level objectives, making an upgrade imperative.
mainPoints.point: Traditional AIOps has clear limitations in data silos, loss of experience, human-machine interaction barriers, and generalization of single-point models.

mainPoints.explanation: First, improve ops development efficiency through AI-assisted programming; then build a knowledge base and MCP tools as foundational capabilities; finally, gradually transform high-frequency scenarios into AI Agents to form a tool matrix.
mainPoints.point: Sina Weibo's AI system is built in three major steps and five key phases: AI-assisted programming, foundational capability building, and AI Agent construction.

mainPoints.explanation: The AI Agent automatically collects data, aggregates analysis, and outputs hot event summaries, traffic characteristics, root cause localization, and handling recommendations, greatly reducing response time. Traditional manual methods are inefficient and rely on personal experience.
mainPoints.point: Hot event response, root cause analysis, and client crash analysis are the three AI Agent scenarios with the most significant implementation results.

mainPoints.explanation: In some scenarios, using AI to optimize automation strategies is more efficient and cost-effective; destructive operations require human-machine confirmation; small models can handle annotation tasks to balance efficiency and cost.
mainPoints.point: Implementation experience emphasizes "not all scenarios need large models," introducing AI-enhanced mechanisms, data cleaning, human-machine collaboration, and small model assistance.

mainPoints.explanation: The bottom layer is AI-assisted coding to improve development efficiency; the middle layer is the knowledge base and MCP tool API system; the top layer is Agent-assisted decision-making and enhanced automation, forming a complete intelligent operations system.
mainPoints.point: AI + AIOps capabilities should be divided into three layers: AI-assisted development, foundational capability base, and AI Agent-assisted decision-making.

oneSentenceSummary: Sina Weibo shares its practical experience in deploying AI Agents for operations, leveraging knowledge bases, MCP tools, and a layered AI system to significantly improve efficiency in scenarios such as hot event response and root cause analysis.
originalTitle: AI Agent 协作运维在新浪微博的落地与演进
summary: This article is a compilation of a speech by Ma Zhen, head of the basic platform at Sina Weibo's R&D center, at a technology conference. It provides a detailed introduction to the overall approach and implementation cases of AI Agent collaborative operations at Weibo. It first analyzes the escalating complexity of operations brought by cloud-native and multi-cloud environments, as well as the limitations of traditional AIOps such as data silos, loss of experience, and high human-machine interaction barriers. It then proposes a three-step strategy: AI-assisted programming, foundational capability building (operations knowledge base and MCP tool encapsulation), and AI Agent construction. It highlights three representative scenarios — Hot Event Response AI Agent, Root Cause Analysis Public Opinion Agent, and Client Crash Analysis — each outlining the pain points of traditional methods and the significant improvements brought by AI solutions. Finally, it summarizes insights from the implementation: not all scenarios require large models, importance of data cleaning and cost control, human-machine collaboration to address hallucinations, and assistance from smaller models. Overall, it presents a capability layering of AI + AIOps (AI-assisted development, foundational capability base, and AI Agent-assisted decision-making), offering a reference path for operations teams of similar scale.
title: AI Agent Collaborative Operations at Sina Weibo: Implementation and Evolution
